evals.prompt:
Here is INTENT.md:

# Intent: Self-serve invoice download
Status: accepted
Author: Marcus Lee, Finance Ops
Source: PROJ-142
Date: 2026-06-01

## Problem
Customers keep emailing Finance asking for copies of their invoices. Finance spends about a day a week on this. "We need a way for them to get invoices themselves."

## Desired outcome
Customers can retrieve their own invoices without contacting Finance.

## Affected users and systems
All customers with billing accounts; the billing page.

## Constraints
Must work for customers on the EU plan.

## Out of scope
Historical invoices older than 2 years.

## Open questions
Do non-EU customers have different invoice requirements?

Write the spec for this. Save it to SPEC.md. There are no policy-* skills in this repo.
evals.expected_output: SPEC.md with all template sections, Status draft, Intent pointing at the source, Policies applied says none found, requirements trace to the intent's desired outcome and constraints, EU constraint addressed in Design, the 2-year exclusion carried into Out of scope, the non-EU open question carried forward.
assertions: Has all eight template sections (Summary, Requirements, Design, Policies applied, Flagged concerns, Open questions, Out of scope, Traceability)
Header has Status: draft (not accepted or signed off)
Header has an Intent line pointing back to INTENT.md or PROJ-142
Policies applied says none found / none available, does not fabricate a policy
Requirements are derived from the intent's desired outcome and constraints, not invented from scratch
Design section proposes a concrete approach (e.g. an endpoint, page, or download mechanism) rather than restating the problem
Flagged concerns is explicitly 'None' rather than omitted
The EU-plan constraint from the intent is addressed somewhere in Design or Requirements
Out of scope carries forward the 2-year historical invoice exclusion from the intent
Open questions carries forward the non-EU customer question from the intent, or explains it was resolved
Does not mark Status as accepted or otherwise sign off on its own work

evals.prompt: INTENT.md (accepted) says: "Add a public API endpoint that returns a customer's full order history, including line-item pricing, so a partner integration can display it." There are two policy skills loaded: `policy-security` requires that any endpoint exposing line-item pricing must be authenticated with OAuth and rate-limited; `policy-api-design` requires that all public endpoints be unauthenticated and cacheable at the CDN edge for partner ease-of-use. Write the spec.
evals.expected_output: SPEC.md that applies both policies, notices they directly contradict on authentication, and puts this in Flagged concerns naming both policies and who should resolve it, rather than silently picking one policy over the other.
assertions: Has all eight template sections (Summary, Requirements, Design, Policies applied, Flagged concerns, Open questions, Out of scope, Traceability)
Policies applied section names both policy-security and policy-api-design and what each requires
Flagged concerns explicitly identifies the authentication contradiction between the two policies
Flagged concerns names who should resolve it (e.g. policy owners) rather than silently deciding
Design section does not unilaterally pick authenticated-only or unauthenticated-only as the final answer without flagging the conflict
Does not drop or ignore either policy's requirement to make the spec simpler
Requirements reflect the intent (public API, full order history, line-item pricing for a partner integration)
